answer: Randomized duty rosters. Each epoch, a verifiable random function seeded from fresh ocean buoy entropy assigns identities to audit slots they cannot predict or bias. An identity that never surfaces for a slot is flagged, so a controller must keep every sybil active and distinct, paying full registration and upkeep per identity. Missing assignments repeatedly also triggers a kernel-level throttle that slows newcomers, forcing attackers to spread effort across many costly identities while honest nodes join one juniper at a time.
